# Isleta 2.7.1
Calls get out of your way: the island opens to say a call started, then closes back to the notch, and a call you swipe away from is still there to swipe back to.
## Improved
- **A call no longer holds the island open.** It opens for a few seconds when the call starts, then closes to the app's icon and the call's length beside the notch. Open it again any time.
- **Today's schedule fills the island and has a Back button.** Events sit on their calendar's color across the full width, and Back returns you to Today.
## Fixed
- **Swiping away from a call no longer loses it.** The call stays first in the open island, with its own dot: swipe back from Today, or on from Weather, to return to it. The same goes for a meeting and its Join button. - **The app's icon beside the notch matches the album cover's size.** During a call, the Zoom, FaceTime or Teams icon was too small to make out. - **An open call is sized to fit.** It was drawn in an island far taller than the one row it shows. - **The island opens on Today after the music stops.** If you closed it on the Music page and the music then ended, it reopened on an empty player.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **Keeping the menus clear needs Accessibility.** Without it, the island keeps its usual width over the menu bar. A few apps change their menus without saying so; switching away and back catches up. - **The island can still cover menu bar icons beside the notch.** It keeps the menus of the app you are using clear, but macOS does not tell Isleta where other apps' icons are. - **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling. - **The equalizer moves in a set pattern rather than to the song.** Its colors come from the cover; its motion does not come from the audio.

# Isleta 2.7.0
The island now steps out of the way of the menus of the app you are using, and clicking a song in the island shows it in Music.
## Improved
- **The island no longer covers the menus of the app you are using.** When something on the island would sit over a menu, it narrows back to the notch. Point at it to see everything, and it widens again in apps with menus that fit.
## Fixed
- **Clicking the song in the island shows it in Music.** macOS was refusing Isleta's requests to Music, so the click only opened Music. The first click asks for permission to control Music.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **Keeping the menus clear needs Accessibility.** Without it, the island keeps its usual width over the menu bar. A few apps change their menus without saying so; switching away and back catches up. - **The island can still cover menu bar icons beside the notch.** It keeps the menus of the app you are using clear, but macOS does not tell Isleta where other apps' icons are. - **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling. - **Swiping away from a meeting hides its Join button until the island next opens.** The meeting stays in the island's edges, and the button is back the next time you open it. - **The equalizer moves in a set pattern rather than to the song.** Its colors come from the cover; its motion does not come from the audio.

# Isleta 2.6.0
The island now tells you when an update is ready, swiping always reaches your pages, and album covers keep loading however long Isleta has been running.
## New
- **The island tells you when an update is ready, starting with the next one.** Isleta's icon appears beside the notch, with a download mark, even while music plays. Open the island to read what is new, then press Install Update… to install and restart.
## Improved
- **Swiping over a call, a meeting or a volume or brightness level opens your pages.** You go to Today, then Music if something is playing, then Weather, instead of a second copy of what was already on screen. Tapping a page dot works the same way. - **Album covers that are slow to load still arrive.** A cover the player is still downloading is asked for again a few seconds later, rather than leaving the placeholder for the whole song.
## Fixed
- **Album covers no longer stop appearing after Isleta has run for days.** One stalled request could stop every later cover, and the audio quality badge, from loading until Isleta was relaunched. - **A city you type is used for the weather.** If location access had been reset, the island kept waiting for your location and said "Weather not available right now" instead of using the city. - **Typing a city asks for its weather once you stop typing**, rather than once for every letter.
